title: Interpretations comparison grid
subject: History
source: Seeded from history/y7 lesson 7 (Interpretations comparison grid (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 7: The journey and the capture of Jerusalem, 1099. To understand how the crusaders reached and captured Jerusalem and how historians interpret the violence

questions.q: Put in order: Antioch, Jerusalem, Constantinople, Nicaea.
questions.model: They met first at Constantinople. Then crossed to Nicaea. Then Antioch. Last, Jerusalem.

questions.q: Name two challenges on the journey.
Why might a crusader chronicler and a Muslim historian describe 1099 differently?
questions.a: Different sides, purposes and distance in time

questions.q: Core: Make an annotated map of the route to Jerusalem with five places and one challenge at each.
questions.a: Constantinople, Nicaea, Dorylaeum, Antioch, Jerusalem with challenges such as hunger, battle, heat
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: dot at Antioch, label 'long siege 1097 to 1098: hunger and disease'.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain why the interpretations of 1099 differ.
questions.a: Writers were on different sides, wrote at different times and had different purposes, so they chose and exaggerated different details

questions.q: Stretch: What was set up after 1099?
questions.a: Crusader states: the Kingdom of Jerusalem, Antioch, Edessa and Tripoli
Surrounding a place to force it to surrender
options: Surrounding a place to force it to surrender

questions.q: Big question: why do accounts of the capture of Jerusalem disagree?
questions.a: The writers were on different sides, wrote at different times and had different purposes
